**Published online:**
Aug 28, 2026

**Geographic focus:**
Asia — India (Mumbai); with secondary reference to US (Jackson Hole / Federal Reserve)

**Temporal focus:**
T1. Historical report [YES] — covers Friday's rupee session and weekly performance
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — Warsh speech impact, MSCI rebalancing (Aug 31), end of RBI deposit window (Monday), Fed policy direction
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

**Synopsis:**
The rupee gained on Friday (+0.2%), closing a positive week, driven by dollar inflows ahead of the RBI's closing non-resident deposit window, MSCI index rebalancing flows (Aug 31), and state-bank offers. RBI's swap facility flexibility is expected to prevent excess dollar liquidity from persisting. The key forward risk is Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole speech: markets want clarity on his inflation and policy stance amid bond market turbulence. A hawkish surprise would pressure the rupee; a dovish tone would ease it. Consensus leans neutral, but uncertainty is elevated given Warsh's reluctance to offer forward guidance.

Relevance: YES — The article directly references Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole speech, Fed policy on persistent inflation, bond market turbulence, and the dollar's reaction function to Fed tone. These are material inputs to US rates pricing and USD direction.

**Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?**
Sentiment: +15 (marginally hawkish lean) — Elevated inflation data is cited, Warsh is known to resist forward guidance, and bond market turbulence is an active concern. While the consensus expects a neutral speech, the inflation backdrop and Warsh's non-committal posture introduce a hawkish skew relative to prior expectations. The article does not signal imminent cuts; the risk framing is asymmetric toward tightening surprise.
